title: Drying principles and monitoring logs
audience: Coordinators, supervisors and trained workers who may be asked about, triage, refer or document cleaning and water-removal work after a flood or water event. Not a qualification or authority to enter a flood-affected building, energise its systems, or certify it as dry, safe or habitable.
learningOutcomes: Explain why drying is a measured trend, and document monitoring without setting universal pass thresholds.

instruction.heading: Scope and authority
instruction.body: This lesson teaches how drying is tracked as a measured trend, and how a monitoring chart and an escalation notice are kept. It does not set pass thresholds, and it does not state that drying is complete. Completing it does not give a licence, certificate or approval.

instruction.heading: Drying principles and monitoring logs
instruction.body: Restoration progress is a measured trend, not simply a finish that looks dry. Covering a surface too early can trap moisture and hide damage. Prepare a monitoring chart and an escalation notice for any moisture that remains unresolved. Do not set universal pass thresholds in a training or operational document, because the appropriate values depend on the material, the method and the building, and must come from the competent professional. Document any ongoing moisture and prevent premature reinstatement of finishes.

procedure: Prepare a monitoring chart with the material, the method, the locations and the dates.
Record each reading as a point on the trend, with its method.
Record the conditions around each reading, so that the trend can be interpreted.
Do not cover or seal a surface until the competent professional has confirmed the trend.
Raise an escalation notice for any moisture that remains unresolved.
Hold reinstatement of finishes until the trend is confirmed in writing.

workedExamples.situation: A plasterer wants to line a wall that the monitoring chart shows is still losing moisture.
workedExamples.reasoning: Stop. Escalate the unresolved moisture and do not line the wall. Covering it now can trap moisture and hide damage.

workedExamples.situation: A job sheet sets a single figure as the drying pass for every material.
workedExamples.reasoning: No. Thresholds depend on the material, the method and the building. They come from the competent professional and are not set in the job sheet.

equipmentAndPpe: Monitoring chart and instruments with calibration records.

commonErrors.error: Covering a damp surface too early, which traps moisture.
commonErrors.prevention: Hold reinstatement until the competent person confirms the trend.

commonErrors.error: Treating a surface as dry because it looks dry.
commonErrors.prevention: Use the monitoring trend, not appearance.

commonErrors.error: Setting a universal pass figure in a job sheet.
commonErrors.prevention: Thresholds come from the competent professional for the material and method.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: This lesson sets no pass threshold. Completing it does not give a licence, certificate or approval.
Covering a damp surface can trap moisture and hide damage.

qualityStandard: The learner tracks drying as a trend, with the method recorded for each reading.
The learner holds reinstatement while moisture is unresolved.
summary: Drying is a trend, not a finish.
Hold reinstatement until the trend is confirmed.

knowledgeChecks.question: A surface is covered with new lining while it is still damp. What is the risk?
options: Moisture can be trapped and damage concealed. Monitor the trend and do not reinstate until a competent person confirms it.
None, because the lining protects the surface from the air and any further damage that might occur later on
The lining will dry the surface faster, since it holds the heat in and speeds up the whole drying process

knowledgeChecks.question: What does drying progress represent in this lesson?
options: A measured trend that a competent person interprets
A fixed number taken from any chart

moduleAuthority.heading: Module authority and restricted work
moduleAuthority.body: This module is training content. It does not grant authority to enter a flood-affected building, to carry out regulated flood restoration, to energise or isolate electrical, gas or solar systems, to remove sewage or contaminated water, to dispose of waste, or to certify that a property is dry, hygienic, structurally sound or safe to occupy. Completing this lesson does not give a licence, certificate or approval. Some of the work described is restricted to licensed, authorised or specially trained people, including electrical and gas work, structural assessment, sewage handling and some disposal. The site controller, the owner, the insurer and the competent professionals each hold separate decisions, and none of them replaces the others. Where the controlling authority or the competent professional is not identified, stop and refer.

stopWorkAndReferral.heading: Stop-work and referral rules for this module
stopWorkAndReferral.body: Stop and refer whenever any of these is true: permission to enter or written safety clearance is missing; the contamination is unknown; a structural hazard, a slip or a confined space has not been cleared; an electrical, gas or solar system is water-exposed or has not been licensed for re-energisation; an exposure has occurred or controls are not in place; the equipment or operators are not suitable; porous material is in question; hidden microbial contamination is suspected; a waste route is not yet known; or a party asks for a dry, hygienic or occupancy statement. A stop-work decision is correct. Record it, and restart only after the competent party has confirmed the scope in writing.
